topic: Can MVDR beamforming sufficiently compensate for pattern degradation in array-fed reflectors during element failures?
consensus_response: MVDR beamforming can mitigate gain loss due to element failures, but its performance depends on covariance matrix estimation accuracy. The defocused reflector concept offers improved robustness against feed element failures due to its reduced sensitivity to spacing between feed elements. However, it comes with limitations such as gain roll-off towards the borders of the illuminated domain. Frequency-selective beamforming can be used to adjust weights based on frequency-dependent array factors, minimizing gain loss while maintaining desired radiation patterns.
reference_context: The defocused reflector concept offers improved robustness against feed element failures due to its reduced sensitivity to spacing between feed elements. A curved feed array approach can provide a viable solution to compensate for the gain roll-off towards the borders of the illuminated domain.
